prompt: What are the coordinates of the point on the unit circle at $180^\circ$?
hint: $180^\circ$ is a half turn — you end up pointing in the exact opposite direction from where you started.

hints.text: $180^\circ$ is a half turn — you end up pointing in the exact opposite direction from where you started.
Starting at $(1, 0)$ and turning halfway around puts you on the negative $x$-axis.

explanation: Half a turn from the positive $x$-axis lands on the negative $x$-axis.
On a circle of radius 1, that point is $(-1, 0)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The four quarter-turn points
steps: Going counterclockwise, the axis points are $(1,0)$ at $0^\circ$, $(0,1)$ at $90^\circ$, $(-1,0)$ at $180^\circ$, and $(0,-1)$ at $270^\circ$.
They cycle: right, up, left, down. $180^\circ$ is the "left" one.
